target.title: fix(agents): remove abort listener on early reject paths in ls tool
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createLsToolDefinition` registers an `onAbort` handler on the caller's `AbortSignal` at line 127 to reject the pending promise with `"Operation aborted"` when the signal fires. The handler is properly cleaned up in the success path (line 185) and the catch block (line 221), but three early-rejection code paths call `reject(...)` without first removing the listener:

- `Path not found` (line 136)
- `Not a directory` (line 143)
- `Cannot read directory` (line 153)

## Why This Change Was Made

The abort listener closure captures `resolve`, `reject`, `cwd`, and other local variables. When the signal never fires, the listener reference keeps this closure alive until the signal object is garbage collected. While `{ once: true }` ensures the listener self-cleans on first abort invocation, the listener leaks when the promise is rejected synchronously and the signal is never aborted.

Adding `signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort)` before each early `reject()` call matches the existing cleanup pattern already used by the success and catch paths.

## User Impact

No behavioral change. The listener cleanup is a resource-management improvement — the three early-rejection paths now properly release their reference to the `AbortSignal`, matching every other exit path in the same function.

## Evidence

Verified against commit `86c47102` on branch `fix/ls-abort-listener-leak`.

### Sibling pattern in `find.ts`

The sibling tool `sessions/tools/find.ts` uses a `settle()` wrapper that centralizes cleanup — every `reject()` and `resolve()` goes through `settle()`, which unconditionally removes the abort listener:

```typescript
// find.ts:179-186 — all paths clean up via settle()
let settled = false;
const settle = (fn: () => void) => {
  if (settled) return;
  settled = true;
  signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
  fn();
};
```

`ls.ts` does not have this wrapper, so each exit path is responsible for its own cleanup. The success path and catch block do it; three early-rejection paths did not.

### Fix

The three added lines mirror the exact same call used at:

```typescript
// line 185 (success path)
signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);

// line 221 (catch block)
signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
```

Each inserted before `reject(...)` in the early-return path. The `signal?.` optional chaining is safe when `signal` is `undefined`.

### Tests

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/agent-tools.read.arg-value-suffix.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       3 passed (3)
```

## Risk Checklist

- **User-visible behavior:** No — zero behavioral change.
- **Config/env/migration behavior:** No.
- **Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution:** No.
- **Plugins/providers/channels/SDK:** No — internal to `ls` tool definition.
- **Highest-risk area:** None. The change is purely additive cleanup; `removeEventListener` is a no-op when the listener has already been removed or the signal is `undefined`.
- **Mitigation:** Follows the existing cleanup pattern from line 185 and line 221.

Closes: N/A
